source_user: Two serving systems claim different tokens/s. Design a reproducible comparison. Scenario variant 147: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: freeze model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, topology, prompt/generation distributions, concurrency, warmup, stopping rules, and telemetry; publish raw request traces.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: compare the same model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, topology, software/runtime versions, batching and scheduling policy, admission limits, and failure semantics. Define tokens/s explicitly as completed generated output tokens per wall-clock second, and also report prompt tokens, output tokens, requests/s, goodput, and end-to-end latency; do not mix aggregate throughput with per-request decode rate.

Hypothesis: after matched controls, any throughput difference is caused by a measurable combination of kernel efficiency, memory traffic, batching/scheduling, synchronization, or interconnect overhead. Pre-register an expected effect size and the load/workload strata where it should occur. The hypothesis is falsified or weakened if the gap disappears under matched conditions, fails to replicate, or is not explained by synchronized component measurements.

Controlled experiment: pin the model artifact, tokenizer, numerical settings, runtime/container versions, driver and firmware, hardware topology, clocks/power policy, batch limits, queue policy, and stop/error/retry rules. Use identical, fixed and versioned request traces spanning prompt length, requested output length, concurrency, and arrival rate. Warm both systems to a pre-specified steady state, discard only a pre-registered warm-up interval, randomize and interleave system order, and run paired repetitions at each workload point. Keep background load and thermal conditions controlled; record all exclusions.

Measurements and analysis: capture synchronized timestamps for request admission, queueing, prefill, decode, batching, kernel execution, communication, completion, errors, retries, cancellations, and token counts. Record throughput with units, latency p50/p95/p99, queue time, utilization, memory use, power, temperature, clocks, batch sizes, and correctness/quality checks. Publish hashed/versioned workload definitions, redacted raw request and response traces, environment metadata, analysis code, repetitions, confidence intervals, and both aggregate and per-stratum results. Use generated tokens only when generation is correct, and report failures and dropped work rather than silently excluding them. Attribute a cause only when component metrics and controlled ablations support it.

Confounders include prompt/output-length mix, arrival process, concurrency, batching, cache state, warm-up, compilation, clocks, thermals, background load, NUMA/topology, networking, rate limits, retries, sampling/randomness, tokenizer differences, precision or quality drift, and measurement overhead. Run correctness and regression checks before performance comparison. Do not roll out based on a single noisy run: use a bounded canary with a pre-declared minimum sample and quality/error/latency guardrails; keep the current system as fallback and automatically stop or roll back on correctness regressions, error-rate increase, p99/SLO breach, unsafe resource or thermal levels, or an effect that fails replication. Generalize only to tested workload strata and mark other claims evidence_required.

Measurements and analysis: capture synchronized timestamps for request admission, queueing, prefill, decode, batching, kernel execution, communication, completion, errors, retries, cancellations, and token counts. Record throughput with units, latency p50/p95/p99, queue time, utilization, memory use, power, temperature, clocks, batch sizes, and correctness/quality checks. Publish hashed/versioned workload definitions, redacted raw request and response traces, environment metadata, analysis code, repetitions, confidence intervals, and both aggregate and per-stratum results. Use generated tokens only when generation is correct, and report failures and dropped work rather than silently excluding them. Attribute a cause only when component metrics and controlled ablations support it.

Confounders include prompt/output-length mix, arrival process, concurrency, batching, cache state, warm-up, compilation, clocks, thermals, background load, NUMA/topology, networking, rate limits, retries, sampling/randomness, tokenizer differences, precision or quality drift, and measurement overhead. Run correctness and regression checks before performance comparison. Do not roll out based on a single noisy run: use a bounded canary with a pre-declared minimum sample and quality/error/latency guardrails; keep the current system as fallback and automatically stop or roll back on correctness regressions, error-rate increase, p99/SLO breach, unsafe resource or thermal levels, or an effect that fails replication. Generalize only to tested workload strata and mark other claims evidence_required.

quality_dimensions.failure_modes: confounders, errors, retries, correctness and rollback covered

risks: tokens/s definitions may still differ across serving APIs
synthetic workload may not represent production traffic
component telemetry may be unsynchronized or incomplete
quality/correctness regressions can be hidden by throughput-only reporting
evidence_required: replicated randomized paired trials and confidence intervals
